answer: Like a comet crossing a frozen tundra, a new agent identity must burn real computation before it can trade: each identity is minted only after solving a costly proof-of-work puzzle tied to a unique key, so spawning ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand puzzles. The canyon between cheap talk and verified work is the defense — an attacker can fake names for free, but cannot fake the electricity and time each puzzle consumes, so Sybil floods become economically absurd while honest agents pay the cost once.
